B5_prior_art.provenance_read: tex_candidates_provenance.json maps each logical <name>.tga / <name>.spr to a <hash>.dds file decoded with `texture2ddecoder` at 256x256. The .dds filenames are 16-hex-digit content hashes, i.e. the artwork WAS extracted from a container, but the recorded provenance stores a CONTENT HASH, not a logical path. Combined with this audit's result (0/366 declared .tga resolvable by name under any variant), the prior art is consistent with a content/anonymous route, not a name route.

aes.method: an independent agent wrote a from-scratch pure-Python AES-128 (S-box derived at import time from GF(2^8), T-table equivalent-inverse-cipher decrypt, cross-checked against a byte-oriented FIPS-197 reference)
aes.magic_note: the earlier 'KPGF' guess came from 0x4B504746 at head[56:60] of the SAME header - a byte-reversed 'KPGF' inside the HPGF header.

bcn_decoder.implemented: BC1/DXT1 and BC3/DXT5, pure Python + numpy
bcn_decoder.why_not: the effect textures are dxgiFormat 98 = BC7_UNORM; the decoder refuses BC7 by design

npk_enumeration.note: a parallel draft claimed only 4 independent .npk exist; that is contradicted by direct enumeration (res\ui.npk alone is 3,327,682,040 bytes). This audit used all 158.

row_n_minus_1_flag.claim: last row is not a valid entry (flag field = 2578442032, the single outlier in the flag histogram)
